slot.brief: Angular momentum of a particle about a point: given position and velocity (or momentum) vectors, compute L = r × p magnitude and direction using the cross product; keep it distinct from the other rotational slot (conservation question).

stem: A particle has position vector $\vec r=(3\hat i+4\hat j)$ m and momentum $\vec p=2\hat k$ kg m s$^{-1}$. Its angular momentum about the origin is
working:
$\vec L=\vec r\times\vec p=(3\hat i+4\hat j)\times2\hat k$\\
$=6(-\hat j)+8\hat i=(8\hat i-6\hat j)$ kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$

Independent check: \(\vec L=\vec r\times\vec p=(3,4,0)\times(0,0,2)=(8,-6,0)\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}\).
solution:
Angular momentum is $�\vec L=\vec r\times\vec p$.
$$\vec L=(3\hat i+4\hat j)\times2\hat k=6(\hat i\times\hat k)+8(\hat j\times\hat k)=8\hat i-6\hat j\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}.$$
